theme: आत्मतृप्ति, निर्लिप्तता, और कर्म से मुक्तता | Self-contentment, detachment, and freedom from need
context: After discussing action without attachment, Krishna describes the rare and steady state of one who has found his grounding in the Self. Such a person is not driven by external validation, approval, or possession; his fullness is inward, and therefore his relation to outer action changes fundamentally.
contextHindi: कर्म को निष्काम भाव से करने के बाद कृष्ण अब उस स्थिति की ओर आते हैं जहाँ व्यक्ति आत्मा में स्थिर हो जाता है। ऐसा व्यक्ति बाहरी मान, स्वीकृति या possessions से नहीं चलता; उसका पूर्णत्व भीतर है, इसलिए बाहर के कर्मों से उसका संबंध भी अलग हो जाता है।
sanskritDevanagari:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः |
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ||३-१७||
transliteration:
yastvātmaratireva syādātmatṛptaśca mānavaḥ .
ātmanyeva ca santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate ||3-17||

wordByWord.meaning: one who delights in the Self alone; not seeking fulfillment in external objects.
satisfied within the Self; not dependent on gains, praise, or results.
content in the Self alone; inwardly stable and not restless in the world.
duty, obligation, or appropriate action; here, no binding obligation remains for the self-established one.

spokenHindi: इस श्लोक में कृष्ण एक बहुत गहरी बात कहते हैं: जो मनुष्य आत्मा में रमता है, आत्मा से तृप्त है, और आत्मा में ही संतुष्ट है, उसके लिए बाहरी कामों का कोई दबाव नहीं रहता। यह कोई निष्क्रियता का संदेश नहीं है; यह आत्म-स्थिरता का संदेश है। समझिए, जब भीतर का सच्चा आधार स्थिर हो जाए, तो जीवन की दौड़ में लोग अक्सर जो दौड़ बनाते हैं—प्राप्ति, लक्ष्य, प्रसिद्धि, परिचितता—उनसे मन की तृप्ति नहीं बंधती। ऐसे व्यक्ति के लिए ‘काम करना है या नहीं करना है’ जैसी बाहरी जंग नहीं रहती, क्योंकि उसकी मुख्य प्रेरणा अब भीतर की शांति है। यह श्लोक हमें सिखाता है कि मुक्ति का अर्थ सिर्फ काम छोड़ना नहीं, बल्कि अपने भीतर के सत्य को पहचानना है।
clearEnglish: This verse describes a state of inward stability rather than mere withdrawal from worldly life. The phrase “delighting in the Self” does not mean becoming an emotional recluse or pretending that society does not matter. It means that the inner center is no longer built on the shifting results of action, praise, fear, or possession. When a person is spiritually grounded, the question “What must I do next?” can become less compulsive and more discerning. The text does not deny action; it says that for the self-established person, action no longer binds the mind in the same way. Inference: the inner source of fulfillment is not an achievement but a recognition of the Self. That does not make the person indifferent to duty; rather, it makes duty less egoic and less gripping. The person remains useful, but no longer defined by outer success.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse states that one who delights in the Self, is satisfied in the Self, and is content within the Self has no obligation in the ordinary sense of worldly action. The emphasis is on inner standing, not on abandoning responsibility by force.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A person who has recognized a deeper source of stability is less controlled by impulsive desire, fear of loss, and craving for approval. This does not mean social inactivity; it means outer action is no longer the center of identity.

interpretationPerspectives.label: COMMENTARY
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The Divine Life Society commentary notes that the sage who rejoices in the Self has no real purpose served by doing or not doing ordinary actions, and no evil touches him through inaction. This is a descriptive spiritual perspective, not a social prescription for every person.

practicalApplication.label: Inner grounding
practicalApplication.text: When a task feels emotionally urgent, pause for ten breaths and ask: am I acting from inner clarity or from the need to be approved, successful, or in control?

practicalApplication.label: No self-made debt
practicalApplication.text: Notice how much of your effort is fueled by comparison. Shift one activity today to being done for calm focus rather than for applause or validation.

reflectionQuestion: When do I treat external success as my real source of peace, and how can I return to the steadiness of the Self?
reflectionQuestionHindi: मैं कब बाहरी सफलता को अपनी वास्तविक शांति का आधार मान लेता हूँ, और मैं अपने भीतर की स्थिरता की ओर कैसे लौट सकता हूँ?
